                "uuid": "01a01fa0-8d02-71b7-bb74-9f78e98c6f71",
                "text": "Oh excellent \u2014 **FacetWP Pro** is a huge upgrade. That's actually the best-in-class filtering solution for WordPress, way ahead of anything else I mentioned. And the Elementor addon means it integrates natively as Elementor widgets instead of shortcodes. You're set up better than I assumed.\n\nLet me recalibrate the plan around FacetWP since it works differently than the free plugins.\n\n## How FacetWP works (mental model)\n\nFacetWP has two core concepts:\n\n1. **Facets** \u2014 the actual filters (a price slider, a category checklist, a search box, a sort dropdown). You create these in `WP Admin \u2192 Settings \u2192 FacetWP`.\n2. **Listing / Template** \u2014 the thing that gets filtered. In your case, this is your **Archive Products widget**.\n\nThe magic: FacetWP automatically detects the WooCommerce product loop on archive pages. So when a user checks a filter, FacetWP AJAX-refreshes just the product grid without reloading the page. No configuration of \"which listing to filter\" needed \u2014 it just works on archive templates.\n\n## Step-by-step: build the filters + sort\n\n### Step 1 \u2014 Kill the ugly toggles (do this first)\n\nIn your Archive Products widget:\n- **Allow Order** \u2192 toggle OFF\n- **Show Result Count** \u2192 toggle OFF\n\nSave. That top bar disappears.\n\n### Step 2 \u2014 Create your facets in FacetWP settings\n\nGo to `WP Admin \u2192 Settings \u2192 FacetWP \u2192 Add New`.\n\nCreate these 4 facets one at a time:\n\n**Facet 1: Categories**\n- Name: `Categories`\n- Facet type: **Checkboxes** (or **Radio** if you want single-select only)\n- Data source: **Taxonomies \u2192 Product categories**\n- Parent term: leave blank\n- Hierarchical: **Yes** (since your 8 are subcategories under one parent)\n- Show ghosts: **Yes** (shows all categories even if zero results after other filters \u2014 better UX)\n- Count: **Yes** (shows \"Devi & Durga (30)\" \u2014 very useful)\n\n**Facet 2: Price**\n- Name: `Price`\n- Facet type: **Number Range** (a slider)\n- Data source: **WooCommerce \u2192 Price** (usually appears as `_price` or similar in the dropdown)\n- Format: `\u20b9%d` (so it shows \u20b9100, \u20b9500 etc.)\n\n**Facet 3: Sort**\n- Name: `Sort`\n- Facet type: **Sort**\n- Add sort options:\n  - Default (as configured)\n  - Newest first (by date, DESC)\n  - Price: Low to High (by price, ASC)\n  - Price: High to Low (by price, DESC)\n  - Name: A-Z (by title, ASC)\n\n**Facet 4: Search (optional but recommended)**\n- Name: `Product Search`\n- Facet type: **Search**\n- Data source: **Post title** + **Post content** (multi-select)\n\nSave each one. Each facet gets a unique \"name\" (slug) that FacetWP uses internally, like `categories`, `price`, `sort`, `product_search`.\n\n### Step 3 \u2014 Place the facets in your Elementor template\n\nSince you have the Elementor addon, you'll see **FacetWP widgets** in the Elementor widget panel. Search \"facet.\"\n\n**Left sidebar (25% column):**\nDrag in FacetWP widgets in this order, selecting the matching facet from each widget's dropdown:\n1. FacetWP \u2013 Selections (shows currently applied filters as removable chips at the top \u2014 great UX)\n2. FacetWP \u2013 Facet \u2192 select `Product Search`\n3. FacetWP \u2013 Facet \u2192 select `Categories`\n4. FacetWP \u2013 Facet \u2192 select `Price`\n5. FacetWP \u2013 Reset button (optional but recommended \u2014 clears all filters)\n\nAdd heading text above each facet for clarity: \"Search\", \"Categories\", \"Price range\".\n\n### Step 4 \u2014 Build your custom sort/count bar above the products\n\nIn the right column, ABOVE the Archive Products widget, add a new **inner section** with 2 columns (50/50 or 60/40):\n\n**Left column:**\n- **Heading widget** with dynamic content: Archive Title (H2, smaller than the main H1, maybe 22px, Fraunces)\n- Below it, a **FacetWP \u2013 Counts widget** \u2014 this displays \"Showing X of Y results\" but you style it yourself. In the widget, use a template like: `Showing [lower]-[upper] of [total] photos`\n\n**Right column (right-aligned):**\n- **FacetWP \u2013 Facet widget** \u2192 select `Sort`\n- Style the dropdown: border, padding, matching typography. Right-align it.\n\nResult: clean bar showing \"Devi & Durga \u00b7 30 photos\" on left, styled sort dropdown on right. Much better than the default.\n\n### Step 5 \u2014 Style everything\n\nFor each FacetWP widget, the Elementor Style tab lets you control:\n- Label typography, color\n- Checkbox/radio size and color\n- Slider track color, thumb color\n- Count text style\n- Spacing between options\n\nMatch to your palette:\n- Accent color for active states: your maroon `#8b1a1a`\n- Labels: DM Sans 14px\n- Facet titles/headings: Fraunces 16px, weight 500\n- Backgrounds: transparent or `#faf8f4`\n\nFacetWP also has its own CSS classes if you want to fine-tune further via Custom CSS \u2014 but Elementor's controls should cover 90%.\n\n### Step 6 \u2014 Mobile handling\n\nFacetWP has a built-in **\"Mobile Flyout\"** feature. Enable it in `Settings \u2192 FacetWP \u2192 Settings tab \u2192 Mobile flyout`. It automatically adds a \"Filter\" button on mobile that opens the facets in a slide-in drawer. Zero extra work, works beautifully.\n\nConfigure:\n- Which facets appear in the flyout (usually all of them)\n- Button label: \"Filters\"\n- Button position: usually top-right of the product grid\n\nThen on mobile, hide the desktop sidebar column (Advanced \u2192 Responsive \u2192 Hide on Mobile).\n\n## The final layout you'll have\n\n```\n\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\nBreadcrumbs\nCategory Title (H1)\nCategory description\n\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\n[Filter Sidebar]  \u2502  Devi & Durga \u00b7 30 photos    [Sort \u25be]\nSearch            \u2502  \u250c\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u252c\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u252c\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2510\nCategories        \u2502  \u2502 P1 \u2502 P2 \u2502 P3 \u2502\n  \u2611 Devi & Durga  \u2502  \u251c\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u253c\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u253c\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2524\n  \u2610 Hanuman       \u2502  \u2502 P4 \u2502 P5 \u2502 P6 \u2502\nPrice range       \u2502  \u2514\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2534\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2534\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2518\n[====\u25cf======]     \u2502  [1] [2] [3]  Next \u2192\n[Reset]           \u2502\n\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\n```\n\n## Start with Steps 1 + 2\n\nTurn off those toggles, then head into `Settings \u2192 FacetWP` and create your first 4 facets. Send me a screenshot when you have the facets created and are ready to place them in Elementor \u2014 I'll help you with the widget placement and styling next.\n\nOne question while you work:\n```\nThis block is not supported on your current device yet.\n```\n\n",

                "uuid": "01a01fa3-2be0-7083-b88e-18fab6e6387f",
                "text": "Let me help you find it. FacetWP's menu location depends on which version/addon you have installed, and it's not always where you'd expect.\n\n## Where to look for FacetWP\n\nTry these locations in order:\n\n**1. Top-level admin menu**\nLook in the left sidebar of WP admin for a menu item literally called **\"FacetWP\"** \u2014 sometimes it appears as its own top-level item, usually near the bottom of the sidebar.\n\n**2. Under Settings**\n`Settings \u2192 FacetWP` \u2014 this is the most common location.\n\n**3. Under Tools**\n`Tools \u2192 FacetWP` \u2014 some versions put it here.\n\n**4. Check if it's actually active**\nGo to `Plugins \u2192 Installed Plugins` and search \"facet\". You should see:\n- **FacetWP** (the main plugin) \u2014 must be **Active**\n- **FacetWP \u2013 Elementor** (the addon) \u2014 must be **Active**\n\nIf either says \"Activate\" instead of \"Deactivate,\" click Activate.\n\n## Did you install the right one?\n\nHere's how to verify. The correct plugins are:\n\n- **Main plugin:** \"FacetWP\" by FacetWP, LLC \u2014 this is the paid core plugin\n- **Elementor addon:** \"FacetWP - Elementor\" by FacetWP, LLC \u2014 this adds the Elementor widgets\n\nBoth should show the author as **FacetWP, LLC** in the plugin list.\n\n**Wrong plugins that people sometimes confuse it with:**\n- \"FacetWP - Free version\" \u2014 this doesn't exist officially; if you see something like this, it's likely a nulled/pirated copy which won't work properly\n- Any plugin with \"Facet\" in the name but different author\n\n## Also check the license\n\nFacetWP is a paid plugin and needs a license key to receive updates and full functionality. Once you find the menu, look for a \"License\" or \"Settings\" tab and confirm the license is activated with a green checkmark or \"Active\" status. Without a valid license, the plugin technically runs but you may lose features.\n\n## If you still can't find it\n\nSend me a screenshot of:\n1. Your `Plugins \u2192 Installed Plugins` page (filter by \"Active\" so I can see what's running)\n2. Your full WP admin left sidebar (scroll all the way down)\n\nI'll spot exactly what's happening.\n\nAlso \u2014 while we're troubleshooting, quick check:\n```\nThis block is not supported on your current device yet.\n```\n\n",

                "text": "Q: Where did you get FacetWP Pro from?\nA: Got it from a bundle (like GPL site)",

                "uuid": "01a01fa4-66c3-7076-876a-0934baec8bb3",
                "text": "Ah, that explains it. Let me be straight with you about this.\n\n## The GPL bundle situation\n\nGPL sites (like FestingerVault, GPLDL, etc.) resell plugins by taking advantage of the GPL license \u2014 technically legal, but there are real trade-offs you should know about:\n\n**What works:**\n- The plugin runs and its features function\n- One-time install and use\n\n**What doesn't work (this is why you might be confused):**\n- **No license activation** \u2014 FacetWP requires a license key from facetwp.com to fully unlock. GPL versions often have this stripped out or return errors.\n- **No updates** \u2014 you're stuck on whatever version the GPL site uploaded. Security issues, bug fixes, WooCommerce compatibility updates \u2014 all skipped.\n- **Menu might be missing** \u2014 some GPL bundlers modify plugin files to bypass license checks, and sometimes they break the admin menu registration in the process. This is likely why you can't find it.\n- **Support cut off** \u2014 no help from FacetWP if something breaks.\n- **Broken addon compatibility** \u2014 the Elementor addon often needs the exact matching version of the core plugin. GPL bundles frequently ship mismatched versions.\n\n## What I recommend you do\n\nHonestly, for a store you're investing real effort into, I'd advise one of two paths:\n\n### Path A \u2014 Buy FacetWP legitimately ($99/year)\n\nIf you love FacetWP's approach, the license pays for itself. You get updates, support, and the menu will actually appear. **Best long-term option** for a serious store.\n\n### Path B \u2014 Switch to a legitimately free plugin (my recommendation for you)\n\nYou're building a store, not testing plugins. Switching to a free-but-genuinely-free alternative removes all the GPL headaches. My picks in order:\n\n1. **FiboFilters** (free) \u2014 modern, AJAX, clean UI, actively maintained. My original recommendation. **This is what I'd use.**\n2. **WOOF** (free) \u2014 powerful, been around forever, well-documented.\n3. **Filter Everything** (free) \u2014 newer, well-designed, has a decent free tier.\n\nAll three give you 90% of what FacetWP offers, for free, forever, with a working menu.\n\n## The GPL trap in general\n\nSince you mentioned bundle sites, one bigger piece of advice: **be very careful with GPL bundles**, especially for things running on your live store. Common problems:\n\n- **Malware injection** \u2014 some GPL sites inject backdoors into plugin files. Not all, but it happens. Your store handles customer data and money.\n- **Nulled versions with hidden ads** \u2014 some inject spam or redirect traffic\n- **Compatibility disasters** \u2014 mixed versions of core plugin + addons cause silent breakage\n\nFor a WooCommerce store that will eventually process real payments and store customer data, I'd strongly encourage you to run only:\n- Free plugins from wordpress.org (official repo)\n- Legitimately purchased premium plugins\n\nYour Elementor Pro, Yoast Pro, CartFlows Pro, LiteSpeed Pro \u2014 hopefully those are all legitimate purchases. If any came from bundles, same warning applies.\n\n## My honest suggestion for right now\n\nDeactivate and delete the GPL FacetWP. Install **FiboFilters** from `Plugins \u2192 Add New \u2192 search \"FiboFilters\"`. It's the closest experience to FacetWP among free options, works great with Elementor (via shortcode or block), and you'll actually be able to find its menu and get updates.\n\nThe tutorial I gave you translates almost directly \u2014 same concepts (create filters, place them in the sidebar, they auto-detect the product loop). Only the menu names and widget names change.\n\n## Your call\n```\nThis block is not supported on your current device yet.\n```\n\n",

                "sender": "human",
                "created_at": "2026-08-20T14:49:12.419984Z",
                "updated_at": "2026-08-20T14:49:12.419984Z",

                "uuid": "01a01fa5-ba7a-728c-b358-2690150dd943",
                "text": "Good call on switching to FiboFilters. Let me address the \"not sure / mixed\" answer first because it matters, then we'll get filters working.\n\n## Quick real-talk on your other plugins\n\nSince you're not sure which are legit and which are GPL, I'd genuinely encourage you to check before you launch this store publicly. Here's a fast way to audit:\n\n**Go to `Plugins \u2192 Installed Plugins`** and for each Pro plugin, look at:\n\n1. **Does it have a working license activation screen?** Go into the plugin's settings \u2014 if it shows \"License Active\" with an email/key, it's legit. If the license field is missing, broken, or says \"License removed\" \u2014 it's GPL.\n2. **Are updates working?** Legit plugins show update notifications when new versions release. GPL ones go silent forever.\n\n**The plugins I'd prioritize being legit for your store:**\n\n- **LiteSpeed Cache** \u2014 actually 100% free from the official repo, no Pro version needed. If someone sold you \"LiteSpeed Pro,\" you got scammed with a rebranded copy. The free version has everything.\n- **Yoast SEO Premium** \u2014 the free Yoast covers 90% of SEO needs. Premium is nice-to-have, not essential. If GPL, just use free Yoast \u2014 safer.\n- **CartFlows Pro** \u2014 GPL versions of CartFlows are common and usually work, but you lose the A/B testing and analytics that make Pro worth it.\n- **Elementor Pro** \u2014 this is the big one. If your Elementor Pro is GPL, that's a real risk because Elementor Pro touches everything on your site. A compromised version could inject malicious code into every page.\n\n**My honest suggestion:** at minimum, buy legit Elementor Pro ($59/yr) since it's the foundation of your entire site. Everything else you can defer or use free alternatives.\n\nNot lecturing \u2014 just want you to know before your store starts taking money.\n\n## Now \u2014 clean up FacetWP and install FiboFilters\n\n### Step 1 \u2014 Remove the GPL FacetWP completely\n\nGo to `Plugins \u2192 Installed Plugins`, find:\n- FacetWP\n- FacetWP - Elementor\n\nFor each: **Deactivate \u2192 Delete**. Both must go.\n\nAlso check `wp-content/plugins/` via your file manager or FTP \u2014 sometimes GPL plugins leave orphan folders. Delete any `facetwp*` folders you see.\n\n### Step 2 \u2014 Install FiboFilters\n\n`Plugins \u2192 Add New \u2192 search \"FiboFilters\"`.\n\nThe correct one:\n- **Name:** FiboFilters \u2013 Fastest and Easiest Filters for WooCommerce\n- **Author:** FiboSoft\n- **Active installations:** 10,000+\n- Should have 5-star reviews and recent updates\n\nInstall \u2192 Activate.\n\n### Step 3 \u2014 Create your first filter group\n\nAfter activation, you'll see a new menu item **\"FiboFilters\"** in the WP admin sidebar.\n\nGo to `FiboFilters \u2192 Filter Groups \u2192 Add New`.\n\nConfigure:\n- **Name:** Shop Filters\n- **Display on:** Shop page + Product category pages (there should be checkboxes for this)\n\nThen add filters inside the group:\n\n**Filter 1 \u2014 Categories**\n- Type: **Checkbox list** (or radio if single-select)\n- Source: **Product categories**\n- Show count: Yes\n- Hierarchical: Yes\n\n**Filter 2 \u2014 Price**\n- Type: **Price slider**\n- Currency prefix: \u20b9\n\n**Filter 3 \u2014 Search** (optional)\n- Type: **Search box**\n\nSave the filter group.\n\n### Step 4 \u2014 Place filters in your Elementor sidebar\n\nFiboFilters primarily works via **shortcode** or an auto-injected sidebar. You have two options:\n\n**Option A \u2014 Shortcode in Elementor (recommended for full control)**\n\nIn your Product Archive template's left column, add a **Shortcode widget** with:\n\n```\n[fibofilters]\n```\n\nThis renders your entire filter group in that spot. Style it via FiboFilters settings + custom CSS.\n\n**Option B \u2014 Auto-inject into theme sidebar**\n\nIn FiboFilters settings, there's an option to auto-inject into the WooCommerce sidebar. Skip this \u2014 it fights with Elementor. Use Option A.\n\n### Step 5 \u2014 Style the filters\n\nFiboFilters has its own **Styling** tab in the plugin settings. You can control:\n- Accent color (set this to your maroon `#8b1a1a`)\n- Border radius\n- Font sizes\n- Checkbox style\n- Slider colors\n\nSet everything to match your DM Sans + maroon palette.\n\nFor deeper styling, add custom CSS in Elementor \u2192 Site Settings \u2192 Custom CSS:\n\n```css\n.fibofilters-filter-title {\n    font-family: 'Fraunces', serif;\n    font-size: 16px;\n    font-weight: 500;\n    color: #1a1a1a;\n    margin-bottom: 12px;\n}\n\n.fibofilters-filter-item label {\n    font-family: 'DM Sans', sans-serif;\n    font-size: 14px;\n}\n\n.fibofilters-count {\n    color: #8a8a8a;\n    font-size: 13px;\n}\n```\n\n### Step 6 \u2014 Sort dropdown\n\nFiboFilters includes a sort shortcode too:\n\n```\n[fibofilters_sort]\n```\n\nPlace this in the top-right of your custom sort/count bar (the one we planned above the products). Style it minimally \u2014 border only, no background, matching typography.\n\n### Step 7 \u2014 Custom count text\n\nFor the \"Devi & Durga \u00b7 30 photos\" line on the left of the sort bar:\n\nUse an Elementor **Heading widget** with dynamic content set to **Archive Title**. Then next to it, a Text widget with the shortcode `[fibofilters_results_count]` if FiboFilters provides one \u2014 or use WooCommerce's default `[woocommerce_result_count]` shortcode.\n\n### Step 8 \u2014 Mobile flyout\n\nFiboFilters has a mobile drawer built in.                         "text": "Good call on switching to FiboFilters. Let me address the \"not sure / mixed\" answer first because it matters, then we'll get filters working.\n\n## Quick real-talk on your other plugins\n\nSince you're not sure which are legit and which are GPL, I'd genuinely encourage you to check before you launch this store publicly. Here's a fast way to audit:\n\n**Go to `Plugins \u2192 Installed Plugins`** and for each Pro plugin, look at:\n\n1. **Does it have a working license activation screen?** Go into the plugin's settings \u2014 if it shows \"License Active\" with an email/key, it's legit. If the license field is missing, broken, or says \"License removed\" \u2014 it's GPL.\n2. **Are updates working?** Legit plugins show update notifications when new versions release. GPL ones go silent forever.\n\n**The plugins I'd prioritize being legit for your store:**\n\n- **LiteSpeed Cache** \u2014 actually 100% free from the official repo, no Pro version needed. If someone sold you \"LiteSpeed Pro,\" you got scammed with a rebranded copy. The free version has everything.\n- **Yoast SEO Premium** \u2014 the free Yoast covers 90% of SEO needs. Premium is nice-to-have, not essential. If GPL, just use free Yoast \u2014 safer.\n- **CartFlows Pro** \u2014 GPL versions of CartFlows are common and usually work, but you lose the A/B testing and analytics that make Pro worth it.\n- **Elementor Pro** \u2014 this is the big one. If your Elementor Pro is GPL, that's a real risk because Elementor Pro touches everything on your site. A compromised version could inject malicious code into every page.\n\n**My honest suggestion:** at minimum, buy legit Elementor Pro ($59/yr) since it's the foundation of your entire site. Everything else you can defer or use free alternatives.\n\nNot lecturing \u2014 just want you to know before your store starts taking money.\n\n## Now \u2014 clean up FacetWP and install FiboFilters\n\n### Step 1 \u2014 Remove the GPL FacetWP completely\n\nGo to `Plugins \u2192 Installed Plugins`, find:\n- FacetWP\n- FacetWP - Elementor\n\nFor each: **Deactivate \u2192 Delete**. Both must go.\n\nAlso check `wp-content/plugins/` via your file manager or FTP \u2014 sometimes GPL plugins leave orphan folders. Delete any `facetwp*` folders you see.\n\n### Step 2 \u2014 Install FiboFilters\n\n`Plugins \u2192 Add New \u2192 search \"FiboFilters\"`.\n\nThe correct one:\n- **Name:** FiboFilters \u2013 Fastest and Easiest Filters for WooCommerce\n- **Author:** FiboSoft\n- **Active installations:** 10,000+\n- Should have 5-star reviews and recent updates\n\nInstall \u2192 Activate.\n\n### Step 3 \u2014 Create your first filter group\n\nAfter activation, you'll see a new menu item **\"FiboFilters\"** in the WP admin sidebar.\n\nGo to `FiboFilters \u2192 Filter Groups \u2192 Add New`.\n\nConfigure:\n- **Name:** Shop Filters\n- **Display on:** Shop page + Product category pages (there should be checkboxes for this)\n\nThen add filters inside the group:\n\n**Filter 1 \u2014 Categories**\n- Type: **Checkbox list** (or radio if single-select)\n- Source: **Product categories**\n- Show count: Yes\n- Hierarchical: Yes\n\n**Filter 2 \u2014 Price**\n- Type: **Price slider**\n- Currency prefix: \u20b9\n\n**Filter 3 \u2014 Search** (optional)\n- Type: **Search box**\n\nSave the filter group.\n\n### Step 4 \u2014 Place filters in your Elementor sidebar\n\nFiboFilters primarily works via **shortcode** or an auto-injected sidebar. You have two options:\n\n**Option A \u2014 Shortcode in Elementor (recommended for full control)**\n\nIn your Product Archive template's left column, add a **Shortcode widget** with:\n\n```\n[fibofilters]\n```\n\nThis renders your entire filter group in that spot.                 "text": "Fair enough \u2014 let me actually look this up properly instead of guessing at outdated syntax.\n```\nThis block is not supported on your current device yet.\n```\n\nOkay, I did the research and I had part of it wrong. Here's the accurate version for FacetWP v4.5, with a critical prerequisite I missed.\n\n## Critical prerequisite first \u2014 WooCommerce setting\n\nFacetWP's Sort facet **will not work** if WooCommerce's default sorting is set to certain options (Popularity, Average Rating, or Sort by price). Only two default sort options are compatible with FacetWP.\n\n**Do this first:**\n1. Go to `Appearance \u2192 Customize \u2192 WooCommerce \u2192 Product Catalog`\n2. Find \"Default product sorting\" dropdown\n3. Set it to one of these two only:\n   - **Default sorting (custom ordering + name)** \u2190 recommended\n   - **Sort by most recent**\n4. Publish\n\nAny other choice and your Sort facet silently breaks. This is FacetWP's #1 gotcha.\n\n## Now the Sort facet configuration\n\nYou're on the right screen. Looking at your screenshot, here's what each field means:\n\n- **Label:** `Sort` (what shows in admin) \u2014 \u2705 correct\n- **Default label:** `Sort by` (placeholder text in the dropdown before user picks) \u2014 \u2705 correct\n- **Sort options:** this is where you add each dropdown choice. **You need to add multiple rows** using the \u2795 button on the right.\n\n## Add these 5 sort options (one row each)\n\nFor each row, fill in: **Label** (left field, what user sees) \u2192 **Orderby** dropdown \u2192 **Order** (ASC/DESC).\n\n**Row 1 \u2014 Sort by newest**\n- Label: `Newest first`\n- Orderby: `Post Date`\n- Order: `DESC`\n\n**Row 2 \u2014 Sort by name A-Z**\n- Label: `Name: A to Z`\n- Orderby: `Post Title`\n- Order: `ASC`\n\n**Row 3 \u2014 Sort by price low to high** (this one's tricky)\n- Label: `Price: Low to High`\n- Orderby: scroll the dropdown down \u2014 you need to find **Custom Field** (below \"Menu Order\" in your dropdown). Select it.\n- A new field appears \u2014 enter meta key: `_price`\n- Field type: select **NUMERIC** (very important \u2014 TEXT will sort wrong)\n- Order: `ASC`\n\n**Row 4 \u2014 Sort by price high to low**\n- Same as Row 3 but Order: `DESC`\n- Label: `Price: High to Low`\n\n**Row 5 \u2014 Default (optional fallback)**\n- Label: `Featured`\n- Orderby: `Menu Order`\n- Order: `ASC`\n\nClick the \u2795 icon after each row to add another.\n\n## Screenshot-specific note\n\nIn your screenshot, the dropdown is showing categories like \"POSTS\" with items like Post Title, Post Name, Post Type, etc. Scroll DOWN in that dropdown \u2014 below Menu Order there should be a \"Custom Field\" option. That's what you use for price sorting.\n\nIf Custom Field isn't visible in the dropdown, scroll or search within the dropdown. It's definitely there in v4.5.\n\n## Warning about your products\n\nYour search result mentioned this and it applies to you: **if any of your products are Variable products (with variations), sorting by price won't work reliably.** For a photo store, your products are likely Simple products (each frame size is a separate product or a single price), so you should be fine. But if you ever add variations, sort-by-price will need custom code.\n\n## After saving\n\n1. Save changes (top right)\n2. Click **Re-index** (also top right) \u2014 mandatory after any facet change\n3. Move on to the Search facet\n\n## For the Search facet (simple)\n\nAdd new facet:\n- Label: `Search`\n- Facet type: **Search**\n- Data source: **Post Title** (or add Post Content if you want fuller matches)\n- Placeholder text: `Search photos...`\n\nSave. Done.\n\n## After all 4 facets exist\n\nRe-index one final time, then head to Elementor to place them.\n\nTry the Sort facet again with these exact settings. If the \"Custom Field\" option genuinely doesn't exist in your dropdown, send a screenshot of the fully-expanded dropdown and I'll find the workaround.",

Before any interaction with the Sort facet, the order of the post listing is determined by the orderby and order parameters that are implicitly or explicitly set for the listing\u2019s query. How you can change this sort order depends on the type of listing template you are using on your page.                         "flags": null,
                        "type": "text",
                        "text": "Okay, I did the research and I had part of it wrong. Here's the accurate version for FacetWP v4.5, with a critical prerequisite I missed.\n\n## Critical prerequisite first \u2014 WooCommerce setting\n\nFacetWP's Sort facet **will not work** if WooCommerce's default sorting is set to certain options (Popularity, Average Rating, or Sort by price). Only two default sort options are compatible with FacetWP.\n\n**Do this first:**\n1. Go to `Appearance \u2192 Customize \u2192 WooCommerce \u2192 Product Catalog`\n2. Find \"Default product sorting\" dropdown\n3. Set it to one of these two only:\n   - **Default sorting (custom ordering + name)** \u2190 recommended\n   - **Sort by most recent**\n4. Publish\n\nAny other choice and your Sort facet silently breaks. This is FacetWP's #1 gotcha.\n\n## Now the Sort facet configuration\n\nYou're on the right screen. Looking at your screenshot, here's what each field means:\n\n- **Label:** `Sort` (what shows in admin) \u2014 \u2705 correct\n- **Default label:** `Sort by` (placeholder text in the dropdown before user picks) \u2014 \u2705 correct\n- **Sort options:** this is where you add each dropdown choice. **You need to add multiple rows** using the \u2795 button on the right.\n\n## Add these 5 sort options (one row each)\n\nFor each row, fill in: **Label** (left field, what user sees) \u2192 **Orderby** dropdown \u2192 **Order** (ASC/DESC).\n\n**Row 1 \u2014 Sort by newest**\n- Label: `Newest first`\n- Orderby: `Post Date`\n- Order: `DESC`\n\n**Row 2 \u2014 Sort by name A-Z**\n- Label: `Name: A to Z`\n- Orderby: `Post Title`\n- Order: `ASC`\n\n**Row 3 \u2014 Sort by price low to high** (this one's tricky)\n- Label: `Price: Low to High`\n- Orderby: scroll the dropdown down \u2014 you need to find **Custom Field** (below \"Menu Order\" in your dropdown). Select it.\n- A new field appears \u2014 enter meta key: `_price`\n- Field type: select **NUMERIC** (very important \u2014 TEXT will sort wrong)\n- Order: `ASC`\n\n**Row 4 \u2014 Sort by price high to low**\n- Same as Row 3 but Order: `DESC`\n- Label: `Price: High to Low`\n\n**Row 5 \u2014 Default (optional fallback)**\n- Label: `Featured`\n- Orderby: `Menu Order`\n- Order: `ASC`\n\nClick the \u2795 icon after each row to add another.\n\n## Screenshot-specific note\n\nIn your screenshot, the dropdown is showing categories like \"POSTS\" with items like Post Title, Post Name, Post Type, etc. Scroll DOWN in that dropdown \u2014 below Menu Order there should be a \"Custom Field\" option. That's what you use for price sorting.\n\nIf Custom Field isn't visible in the dropdown, scroll or search within the dropdown. It's definitely there in v4.5.\n\n## Warning about your products\n\nYour search result mentioned this and it applies to you: **if any of your products are Variable products (with variations), sorting by price won't work reliably.** For a photo store, your products are likely Simple products (each frame size is a separate product or a single price), so you should be fine. But if you ever add variations, sort-by-price will need custom code.\n\n## After saving\n\n1. Save changes (top right)\n2. Click **Re-index** (also top right) \u2014 mandatory after any facet change\n3. Move on to the Search facet\n\n## For the Search facet (simple)\n\nAdd new facet:\n- Label: `Search`\n- Facet type: **Search**\n- Data source: **Post Title** (or add Post Content if you want fuller matches)\n- Placeholder text: `Search photos...`\n\nSave. Done.\n\n## After all 4 facets exist\n\nRe-index one final time, then head to Elementor to place them.\n\nTry the Sort facet again with these exact settings. If the \"Custom Field\" option genuinely doesn't exist in your dropdown, send a screenshot of the fully-expanded dropdown and I'll find the workaround.",

                    }

                "uuid": "01a0227e-0dd3-72ba-906e-b99262182ad7",
                "text": "Hey what according to you is a skills that a digital marketer must have, should have, and could have?",
                "content": [
                    {
                        "start_timestamp": "2026-08-21T04:04:42.442811Z",
                        "stop_timestamp": "2026-08-21T04:04:42.442811Z",
                        "flags": null,
                        "type": "text",
                        "text": "Hey what according to you is a skills that a digital marketer must have, should have, and could have?",
                        "citations": []
                    }
                ],
                "sender": "human",
                "created_at": "2026-08-21T04:04:42.442972Z",
                "updated_at": "2026-08-21T04:04:42.442972Z",
                "attachments": [],

                "parent_message_uuid": "00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000000"
            },
            {
                "uuid": "01a0227e-0dd3-72dc-b715-60b2939d0ffb",
                "text": "Here's how I'd break it down:\n\n**Must have** (core, non-negotiable)\n- Content writing/copywriting \u2014 clear, persuasive copy across channels\n- Analytics literacy \u2014 reading Google Analytics/GA4, interpreting data, drawing decisions from it\n- SEO fundamentals \u2014 keyword research, on-page basics\n- Paid ads basics \u2014 Google Ads, Meta Ads campaign setup and budgeting\n- Social media strategy \u2014 platform-specific content and community building\n\n**Should have** (strongly differentiating)\n- Email marketing/automation (Klaviyo, Mailchimp, HubSpot)\n- Basic design skills \u2014 Canva or Figma, enough for on-brand visuals\n- CRO (conversion rate optimization) \u2014 A/B testing, funnel thinking\n- Marketing automation/CRM tools\n- Storytelling and brand positioning\n\n**Could have** (nice edge, not essential everywhere)\n- Basic coding/HTML \u2014 for landing pages, tracking pixels, troubleshooting\n- Video editing (CapCut, Premiere basics)\n- AI tool fluency \u2014 prompting, workflow automation with tools like this one\n- Influencer/partnership marketing know-how\n- Advanced data skills \u2014 SQL, Python for deeper analysis\n\nThe \"must haves\" apply almost everywhere; the \"could haves\" matter more depending on whether you're in-house, agency, freelance, or a specific niche (B2B vs. e-commerce, for example). If you tell me which direction you're headed, I can prioritize this differently.",

            {
                "uuid": "01a02285-36f6-7246-9122-329846a78614",
                "text": "What you're describing is really common, and it has a name in different fields \u2014 \"the cobbler's children have no shoes.\" There are a few real reasons it happens, and none of them mean you don't actually know your stuff:\n\n**Why this happens**\n\n- **Client work has constraints, your own work doesn't.** When a client hires you, you have a brief, a deadline, a budget, an audience already defined. For yourself, you have infinite options and no external pressure \u2014 and too much freedom is paralyzing. Your brain doesn't know where to start because *everything* is a choice.\n\n- **It's emotionally loaded.** A client's website failing feels like \"the client's problem.\" Your own website failing feels like *you* failing, personally. That fear quietly blocks decision-making \u2014 it's much easier to execute a strategy when your own identity isn't riding on the outcome.\n\n- **Knowing a framework \u2260 having decided who you are.** You can teach keyword research, content pillars, competitor analysis \u2014 all of that is method. But applying it to yourself first requires answering \"who am I, what do I stand for, who exactly am I talking to\" \u2014 and that's a different kind of work (positioning/identity), not a marketing skill gap.\n\n- **Teaching mode and doing mode use different muscles.** Teaching means breaking things into clear, sequenced steps for someone else. Doing means messy, ambiguous, self-directed choice-making. You're excellent at the first; the second has just never been forced on you the same way, because you always had clients' problems to solve instead.\n\n**A way through it**\n\nTreat yourself as a client. Literally. Give yourself a fake brief:\n- Pick one platform, one audience, one goal for 30 days.\n- Write it down like you would for a paying client's contract.\n- Set a content calendar with actual dates \u2014 don't leave \"what to post\" as an open question each day.\n\nThe blankness usually isn't a knowledge problem \u2014 it's a \"too many open decisions, no forcing function\" problem. Constrain it artificially and the paralysis usually breaks.",

                "content": [

                        "flags": null,

                        "text": "Q: Who do you primarily want your LinkedIn content to attract?\nA: Business owners who'd hire me (Ads/SEO/CRO/web clients)",

                ],
                "sender": "human",
                "created_at": "2026-08-21T04:21:13.978086Z",
                "updated_at": "2026-08-21T04:21:13.978086Z",
                "attachments": [],
                "files": [],
                "parent_message_uuid": "01a0228c-e255-726a-95dd-f041a6e4c9aa"

            {
                "uuid": "01a0228d-2f7e-72c1-8f67-07838be0f32f",
                "text": "Good \u2014 that changes the content completely from \"teach marketers frameworks\" to \"show business owners you can make them money.\" Business owners don't care about your process, they care about outcomes and trust. Here's a structure:\n\n**4 content pillars (rotate through these)**\n\n1. **Proof/results** \u2014 before-after of client work: \"This client's CRO fix took conversion from 1.2% to 3.1%. Here's the one change.\" No fluff, just the number and the lever you pulled.\n2. **Mistakes you see** \u2014 \"3 things I see on every SEO audit that's killing rankings\" or \"Why your Google Ads budget is bleeding money.\" Business owners self-select into your audience because they recognize their own site.\n3. **Behind-the-scenes / how you think** \u2014 a screen recording or short breakdown of your actual process (an audit, a CRO teardown of a random website, a keyword gap analysis).                                 "text": "phase3/session_02_summary.md\n# Session 2 Summary \u2014 Batch C, part 1: the four Learn content pillars\n\n**Date:** 19 August 2026\n**Scope produced:** Pages 14\u201317 of 50\n**Status:** All four complete and verified. The structural decision that shaped all four pages\n\n`BLUEPR_3.MD` specifies each Learn pillar as an index \u2014 grouped H2s whose H3s link down to cluster articles. That works when the clusters exist. At launch, they mostly do not:\n\n| Pillar | Clusters the blueprint links | In launch scope |\n|---|---|---|\n| Google Ads | ~17 | **1** |\n| SEO | ~20 | **9** |\n| Web Development | ~15 | **3** |\n| CRO & Automation | ~14 | **3** |\n\nBuilding them as specified would have produced four pages that are mostly signposts to 404s.\n\n**So the structure is preserved and the weight is inverted.** Each H2 now *carries* the substance it would otherwise have delegated. Account structure, negatives, match types, Performance Max, remarketing and diagnostics are answered on the Google Ads pillar. Technical SEO, on-page, schema, architecture and content strategy are answered on the SEO pillar. WordPress speed, Razorpay, security, hosting and e-commerce platform choice are answered on the web development pillar. Landing pages, forms, analytics, attribution and follow-up are answered on the CRO pillar.\n\nThree consequences worth knowing:\n\n- **Each pillar is genuinely self-contained at launch**, which is what a pillar should be anyway. A visitor who lands on one gets a complete answer rather than a table of contents.\n- **Each cluster article, when it publishes, expands a section that already exists** rather than filling a hole. The index sections say plainly that they are short rather than padding with dead links.\n- **`numberOfItems` in each `ItemList` matches the visible links exactly** \u2014 1, 9, 3, 3. There is a build note on the Google Ads pillar, and it applies to all four: increment on every publish. An `ItemList` that drifts out of sync with the page is a worse structured-data signal than none.\n\n---\n\n## 3. Decisions you should review\n\n**The Google Ads pillar links one guide.",

                                "text": "information of vrajvithalani\n***\n\n## Later Web Projects and Tech Stack Evolution  \n\nAfter VGS IT Solution was dissolved (around 30 May 2025), the WordPress clients largely continued with Vraj individually, while the .NET projects effectively ended due to performance and resourcing issues.  \n\nPost\u2011VGS, he continued to build and modernize his stack:  \n- **drvishva.com** \u2013 a physiotherapy website built in Next.js, designed to be fast, SEO\u2011friendly, and conversion\u2011oriented.  \n- **vitthalshringar.com** \u2013 an e\u2011commerce project he\u2019s currently working on (domain finalization and maintenance ongoing).  \n- A planned NGO project \u2013 including a custom CMS for donation and beneficiary management, campaign landing pages, paid ads for fundraising, on\u2011ground volunteering, and compliance/legal record tracking, which he is doing pro bono.  \n\nFor his own brand, he shifted toward a modern stack (Next.js frontend, NestJS backend, MySQL, usually deployed on platforms like Hostinger and Cloudflare) and a clean white/black/soft\u2011teal visual identity that carries across his website and social media content.\n\n***\n\n## ANPR and Embedded Systems  \n\nRecently, Vraj expanded into embedded systems and computer vision, building an **Automatic Number Plate Recognition (ANPR)** system on Raspberry Pi. He architected and implemented a full ANPR pipeline in Python using Raspberry Pi 4 and Pi Camera modules, logging and web\u2011based viewing of detections, and optimizations tailored for CPU\u2011only deployments. [perplexity](https://www.perplexity.ai/search/a32d61af-70dd-4e53-bce3-5c6b283536bc)\n\nHe partnered with the founder of **IOTA**, a company based in Kerala, on a 20% partnership arrangement to develop this ANPR system from scratch in roughly 100 working hours, with the goal of deploying it into a production environment with many gates. The project involves:  \n- Edge processing for license plate detection.  \n- Networked communication between gate devices and a central interface.  \n- A web UI for operators to monitor and manage vehicles.  \n\nWhile some implementation details are confidential, the ANPR project positions him not just as a marketer and web developer, but as someone capable of designing and delivering industrial\u2011style computer vision systems.  \n\n***\n\n## Financial and Business Reality (Sanitized for Public Use)  \n\nRunning VGS IT Solution taught Vraj hard lessons about:  \n- Fixed costs (office rent, staff salaries, infrastructure).  \n- Cash flow challenges when revenue lags behind expenses.  \n- Partnership dynamics and decision\u2011making under age and experience gaps.  \n\nRather than publicly highlighting debts or disputes, his story is best framed as:  \n- A young founder who experienced both client success and operational difficulties.  \n- Someone who took responsibility for closing the company cleanly, settling dues, and transitioning clients.  \n- A professional who then rebuilt his career through teaching, freelancing, and higher\u2011margin marketing and automation services.",

                                "text": "information of vrajvithalani\nHere\u2019s a cleaned, professional introduction of Vraj that you can paste into Claude as persona/context.\n\n***\n\n## Overview  \n\nVraj Vithalani is a full\u2011stack developer, digital marketer, and founder who blends deep technical skills with hands\u2011on marketing execution. He started his journey with a diploma in computer engineering and quickly moved into building real products and client projects instead of staying purely academic.\n\nToday, he positions himself as a specialist in performance marketing (Google Ads, Meta Ads), SEO, CRO, and automation, with a strong secondary profile in Python\u2011based backend development and modern web stacks like Next.js.\n\n***\n\n## Early Entrepreneurship and VGS IT Solution  \n\nIn his very first semester of diploma, Vraj co\u2011founded an IT company named **VGS IT Solution** on 14 December 2023, together with a mentor and another partner. The structure was unusual: the two partners would arrive after their day jobs (around 7\u20138 PM), while Vraj ran the office full\u2011time from around 10 AM to 10 PM, handling most day\u2011to\u2011day operations.  \n\nAt that stage he was primarily:  \n- A WordPress developer, building sites and simple SaaS/CRM\u2011like products.  \n- A Python developer using Django and FastAPI for backend applications and internal tools.  \n\nThe initial strategy was to onboard WordPress projects quickly while trying to attract Python/Django work, but in the local market there was essentially no outsourcing of Python projects, so the company leaned heavily on WordPress and service\u2011based work rather than Python contracts.  \n\n***\n\n## Early Web Projects and End\u2011to\u2011End Ownership  \n\nThe first major client VGS IT Solution acquired was **Dreams Astro Numero Foundation**, an astrology and numerology institute run by astrologer Piyush Nagar (dreamsastronumero.com).  \n\nFor this project, Vraj:  \n- Developed the entire WordPress site focused on courses, consultations, and lead capture.  \n- Managed Hostinger shared WordPress hosting (development, staging/testing, and production deployments).  \n- Handled all client communication, requirement gathering, budgeting, and basic legal formalities, as the other partners were occupied with day jobs.  \n- Integrated Razorpay for payments, including verification and compliance discussions.  \n- Implemented security using WordFence and two\u2011factor authentication.  \n- Configured Google Analytics 4, Google Search Console, and core SEO/meta tag setup.  \n\nThe site included multiple course pages, ~22\u201323 services pages, a full checkout flow, and contact/enrolment funnel \u2013 essentially Vraj\u2019s first legally billed, fully end\u2011to\u2011end project.  \n\nSubsequent WordPress projects included:  \n- **vmgraphiteindustries.com** \u2013 an exporter of graphite suspension and foil tape, where the client provided minimal content and Vraj had to research and shape a complete, coherent website with clean design and structure.",

                                "text": "01_master_narrative.md\n# Vraj Vithalani \u2014 Master Narrative\n\n*Sanitized single-source-of-truth document for website copy. Single-actor framing throughout. No named individuals other than Vraj. Companies named only as clients or collaborators.*\n\n---\n\n## Overview\n\nVraj Vithalani is a full-stack developer, digital marketer, and founder who blends deep technical skills with hands-on marketing execution. He started his journey with a diploma in computer engineering and quickly moved into building real products and client projects instead of staying purely academic.\n\nToday, he positions himself as a specialist in performance marketing (Google Ads, Meta Ads), SEO, CRO, and automation, with a strong secondary profile in Python-based backend development and modern web stacks like Next.js.\n\n---\n\n## Early Entrepreneurship and VGS IT Solution\n\nIn the first semester of his diploma, Vraj founded **VGS IT Solution** on 14 December 2023 and spent the next 18 months running it end-to-end \u2014 from cold calls at 10 AM to deployments at 10 PM. He handled daily operations of the company single-handedly: client acquisition, development, delivery, budgeting, and everything in between.\n\nAt that stage he was primarily:\n- A WordPress developer, building sites and simple SaaS/CRM-like products.\n- A Python developer using Django and FastAPI for backend applications and internal tools.\n\nThe initial strategy was to onboard WordPress projects quickly while trying to attract Python/Django work, but in the local market there was essentially no outsourcing of Python projects, so the company leaned heavily on WordPress and service-based work rather than Python contracts.\n\n---\n\n## Early Web Projects and End-to-End Ownership\n\nThe first major client VGS IT Solution acquired was **Dreams Astro Numero Foundation**, an astrology and numerology institute (dreamsastronumero.com).\n\nFor this project, Vraj:\n- Developed the entire WordPress site focused on courses, consultations, and lead capture.\n- Managed Hostinger shared WordPress hosting (development, staging/testing, and production deployments).\n- Handled all client communication, requirement gathering, budgeting, and legal formalities directly.\n- Integrated Razorpay for payments, including verification and compliance discussions.\n- Implemented security using WordFence and two-factor authentication.\n- Configured Google Analytics 4, Google Search Console, and core SEO/meta tag setup.\n\nThe site included multiple course pages, ~22\u201323 services pages, a full checkout flow, and contact/enrolment funnel \u2014 his first legally billed, fully end-to-end project.\n\nSubsequent WordPress projects included:\n\n- **vmgraphiteindustries.com** \u2014 an exporter of graphite suspension and foil tape, where the client provided minimal content and Vraj had to research and shape a complete, coherent website with clean design and structure.",

                                "text": "BLUEPR_1.MD\n### Global elements\n\n- **Header**: minimal top nav \u2014 logo (wordmark \"Vraj Vithalani\" + soft-teal dot), primary nav (Services \u00b7 Learn \u00b7 Case Studies \u00b7 About \u00b7 Contact), mobile hamburger. Fixed on scroll with translucent white background (glassmorphism).\n- **Footer**: three-column \u2014 (1) Vraj Vithalani NAP + WhatsApp + email, (2) primary nav mirror, (3) legal (Privacy, Terms) + last-updated of site + copyright.\n- **WhatsApp floating CTA**: bottom-right on every page, `https://wa.me/918460474721?text=Hi%20Vraj%20\u2014%20` (pre-filled greeting). Renders as circular button with WhatsApp glyph + subtle bounce on first visit, hidden on scroll-up on mobile to preserve reading space.\n- **Cookie banner**: minimal, functional (GA4 opt-in), dismissible, link to `/privacy/`. Consent stored client-side.\n- **Skip-to-content link**: visible on keyboard focus, accessibility default.\n\n### Typography (proposed \u2014 [TO FINALIZE PHASE 4])\n\n- **Body & UI**: Inter Variable (Google Fonts, self-hosted for speed). Weights loaded: 400, 500, 600, 700.\n- **Display / H1s**: Inter Display (same family, tighter tracking) \u2014 or single-family Inter with letter-spacing tuning if the display variant is unavailable in the chosen stack.\n- **Monospace (code blocks in Learn content)**: JetBrains Mono, weight 400.\n- **Base font size**: 17px on desktop, 16px on mobile. Body line-height 1.6.\n- **Heading scale**: H1 clamp(2.25rem, 4vw, 3.25rem); H2 clamp(1.75rem, 3vw, 2.25rem); H3 1.375rem; H4 1.125rem.\n- Font loading: `font-display: swap`, preload the primary weight.\n\n### Color palette (proposed \u2014 [TO FINALIZE PHASE 4])\n\nAnchored to Doc 02: white base, black, soft-teal accent, glassmorphism-friendly. All values pass WCAG AA at intended usages.\n\n| Token | Hex | Usage |\n|---|---|---|\n| `--ink` | `#0A0A0A` | Body text, primary headings |\n| `--base` | `#FFFFFF` | Page background |\n| `--teal-500` | `#14B8A6` | Primary accent \u2014 link text, primary buttons, focus rings |\n| `--teal-300` | `#5EEAD4` | Highlight tint on glassmorphism surfaces |\n| `--teal-700` | `#0F766E` | Interactive state (hover, active) |\n| `--surface` | `#F8FAFC` | Off-white section backgrounds |\n| `--muted` | `#6B7280` | Secondary text, captions |\n| `--border` | `#E5E7EB` | Card borders, dividers |\n| `--glass` | `rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.55)` + `backdrop-filter: blur(14px)` | Header, cards, testimonial surfaces |\n\n### Accessibility\n\n- WCAG 2.2 Level AA minimum on every page.\n- Keyboard navigation complete: skip link, focus rings visible, no keyboard traps.\n- Alt text on every non-decorative image (decorative images use `alt=\"\"`).\n- Form fields have visible labels, error messages announced via `aria-live`.\n- Colour contrast checked at build time (Lighthouse + axe).\n- Prefers-reduced-motion honoured (glassmorphism animations disable, transitions become instant).\n- Semantic HTML5 landmarks (`header`, `nav`, `main`, `article`, `aside`, `footer`).",

                                "type": "text",
                                "text": "information of vrajvithalani\n- Designed creatives in Canva.  \n- Managed posting schedules and engagement.  \n\nDuring this project he discovered a critical misalignment: the client actually needed **lead\u2011driven paid advertising** (Meta/Instagram ads) for new admissions, whereas his partners had pitched organic social media management. By the time he personally met and clarified the requirements, the client had already onboarded another agency, but his work had still lifted brand awareness roughly 10x (from ~500\u2013600 monthly views to ~5.5\u20136k). This experience strengthened his ability to diagnose real marketing needs rather than just \u201cposting for activity.\u201d  \n\nHe later ran campaigns for:  \n- **VM Graphite Industries** (through the website work).  \n- **Parv Travels**, a tours and travel agency, where he managed performance campaigns for about three months, achieved strong results, and then placed one of his students as a full\u2011time marketer at the agency.  \n- **Synergy Tutorials**, a commerce coaching institute, where he ran ads to drive admissions footfall.  \n\n***\n\n## Teaching and Curriculum Design  \n\nAs his marketing skills grew, Soni Computer Institute invited him to partner as a **digital marketing tutor**, on a 50\u201350 revenue partnership model:  \n- Vraj designed the full curriculum and taught live, practical batches.  \n- The classes provided infrastructure and handled admissions.  \n\nThe office of VGS IT Solution was on the 2nd floor and the classes on the 1st floor of the same building, which made it physically easy for him to switch between company work and teaching.  \n\nHe taught around 20 students, not just theory but complete execution:  \n- Basics of marketing, funnels, and customer psychology.  \n- Performance marketing (Meta Ads, Google Ads).  \n- Creative strategy and idea generation.  \n- Competitor analysis.  \n- SEO and content marketing.  \n- Email and WhatsApp marketing.  \n- WordPress website development and e\u2011commerce.  \n\nHe also actively helped students get jobs or freelancing roles, placing them in SEO, WordPress development, and social media roles at different businesses. This teaching relationship is winding down, and he is scheduled to stop teaching there around 1 August (moving his focus back toward client work and his own brand).  \n\n***\n\n## Later Web Projects and Tech Stack Evolution  \n\nAfter VGS IT Solution was dissolved (around 30 May 2025), the WordPress clients largely continued with Vraj individually, while the .NET projects effectively ended due to performance and resourcing issues.  \n\nPost\u2011VGS, he continued to build and modernize his stack:  \n- **drvishva.com** \u2013 a physiotherapy website built in Next.js, designed to be fast, SEO\u2011friendly, and conversion\u2011oriented.  \n- **vitthalshringar.com** \u2013 an e\u2011commerce project he\u2019s currently working on (domain finalization and maintenance ongoing).",

No contact-form CTA on home.\n\n### Media requirements\n\n- **Hero image**: professional Vraj headshot, medium-wide framing, white or subtle glassmorphism background, soft-teal accent lighting. 1920\u00d71080, WebP + AVIF.                 "text": "Ahh, switching from WordPress to Next JS, interesting pivot.                                 "text": "     1\t---\n     2\tname: docx\n     3\tdescription: \"Use this skill whenever the user wants to create, read, edit, or manipulate Word documents (.docx files) or Word templates (.dotx files). LICENSE.txt has complete terms\n     5\t---\n     6\t\n     7\t# DOCX creation, editing, and analysis\n     8\t\n     9\tA `.docx` is a ZIP archive of XML files. Choose your approach by task:\n    10\t\n    11\t| Task | Approach |\n    12\t|---|---|\n    13\t| **Create** a new document | Write a `docx` (npm) script \u2014 see gotchas below |\n    14\t| **Edit** an existing document | `unzip` \u2192 edit `word/document.xml` \u2192 `zip` (docx-js cannot open existing files) |\n    15\t| **Read** content | `pandoc -t markdown file.docx` |\n    16\t\n    17\t> Script paths below are relative to this skill's directory.\n    18\t\n    19\t## Creating with docx-js \u2014 gotchas\n    20\t\n    21\t`docx` is preinstalled \u2014 do not run `npm install` first; write the script and `require('docx')` directly. Only if that require fails: `npm install docx`. The model knows the API; these are the footguns:\n    22\t\n    23\t- **Page size defaults to A4.** For US Letter set `page: { size: { width: 12240, height: 15840 } }` (DXA; 1440 = 1\u2033).\n    24\t- **Landscape:** pass portrait dimensions and `orientation: PageOrientation.LANDSCAPE` \u2014 docx-js swaps width/height internally.\n    25\t- **Tables need dual widths:** set `columnWidths` on the table AND `width` on every cell, both in `WidthType.DXA` (PERCENTAGE breaks in Google Docs). Column widths must sum to the table width.\n    26\t- **Table shading:** use `ShadingType.CLEAR`, never `SOLID` (renders black).\n    27\t- **Lists:** never insert `\u2022` literally; use a `numbering` config with `LevelFormat.BULLET`.\n    28\t- **`ImageRun` requires `type:`** (`\"png\"`, `\"jpg\"`, \u2026).\n    29\t- **`PageBreak` must be inside a `Paragraph`.**\n    30\t- **Never use `\\n`** \u2014 use separate `Paragraph` elements.\n    31\t- **TOC:** headings must use built-in `HeadingLevel.*`; custom heading styles need `outlineLevel` set or they won't appear.\n    32\t- **Don't use a table as a horizontal rule** \u2014 use a paragraph bottom border instead.\n    33\t- **Dot-leader / right-aligned-on-same-line:** use `PositionalTab` (`alignment: PositionalTabAlignment.RIGHT`, `leader: PositionalTabLeader.DOT`) inside a `TextRun`, not literal `.` or space padding.\n    34\t\n    35\t## Verify the output\n    36\t\n    37\tAfter writing a `.docx`, render it and look at it:\n    38\t\n    39\t```bash\n    40\tpython scripts/office/soffice.py --headless --convert-to pdf output.docx\n    41\tpdftoppm -jpeg -r 100 output.pdf page\n    42\tls page-*.jpg   # then Read the images\n    43\t```\n    44\t\n    45\t`pdftoppm` zero-pads page numbers to the width of the page count (`page-01.jpg`\u2026`page-12.jpg`).\n    46\t\n    47\t## Editing existing documents\n    48\t\n    49\tLegacy `.doc` files must be converted first: `python scripts/office/soffice.py --headless --convert-to docx file.doc`.\n    50\t\n    51\t```bash\n    52\tunzip -q doc.docx -d unpacked/\n    53\tfind unpacked -type l -delete   # strip symlink entries \u2014 docx from external parties is untrusted\n    54\tpython scripts/merge_runs.py unpacked/   # coalesce fragmented runs so text is findable\n    55\t# edit unpacked/word/document.xml in place \u2014 do NOT reformat or pretty-print\n    56\t(cd unpacked && rm -f ../out.docx && zip -Xr ../out.docx .)\n    57\tpython scripts/office/validate.py out.docx --original doc.docx   # XSD checks; --auto-repair fixes common issues\n    58\t# redlining? add --author \"<the name you redlined under>\" to check every edit is tracked\n    59\t```\n    60\t\n    61\tWord splits text across many `<w:r>` runs (revision ids, spell-check markers), so a phrase you can see in the document often doesn't exist as a contiguous string in the XML. `merge_runs.py` merges adjacent identically-formatted runs in `word/document.xml` without changing content or rendering; it also accepts a `.docx` directly (`python scripts/merge_runs.py doc.docx -o merged.docx`).\n    62\t\n    63\t**Tracked changes:** when redlining, validate with `--author \"<the name you redlined under>\"` (needs `--original`) \u2014 it reports any text you changed without a `<w:ins>`/`<w:del>` around it, which is easy to do by accident and invisible in the accepted view. Wrap runs in `<w:ins>`/`<w:del>` with `w:id`, `w:author`, `w:date` attributes. Inside `<w:del>`, the text element is `<w:delText>`, not `<w:t>`. A deleted paragraph mark (`<w:pPr><w:rPr><w:del w:id=\"..\" w:author=\"..\" w:date=\"..\"/></w:rPr></w:pPr>`) means \"merge this paragraph into the next\" \u2014 so deleting a paragraph outright is that plus a `<w:del>` around every run. The `<w:del/>` must come before the rPr's other children; their order is schema-enforced.\n    64\t\n    65\tTo produce a clean copy with all tracked changes accepted: `python scripts/accept_changes.py in.docx out.docx`.\n    66\t\n    67\tAccepting a deleted paragraph mark should join that paragraph to the one below it, so a paragraph whose runs are *all* deleted vanishes. Word does this; `accept_changes.py` and `pandoc --track-changes=accept` don't always. Both fail the same way \u2014 they strip the deleted text but leave the emptied paragraph behind, which reads as a stray empty bullet when it was auto-numbered:\n    68\t\n    69\t- `pandoc --track-changes=accept` never joins the paragraphs.\n    70\t- `accept_changes.py` (LibreOffice) joins them correctly, except when the deleted paragraph is followed by an empty spacer paragraph.\n    71\t\n    72\tAn empty bullet in either view is an artifact of that view, not a defect in the document. Check paragraph deletions in the XML.\n    73\t\n    74\t## Comments\n    75\t\n    76\tComments require six cross-linked files. Use the helper \u2014 directory mode when you'll also be editing `document.xml` (saves an unzip/rezip cycle), `.docx`-direct mode otherwise:\n    77\t\n    78\t```bash\n    79\t# Against an already-unpacked directory (preferred when also placing markers)\n    80\tpython scripts/comment.py unpacked/ \"Fees & expenses cap is too low\"\n    81\tpython scripts/comment.py unpacked/ \"Agreed\" --parent 0\n    82\t\n    83\t# Against a .docx directly\n    84\tpython scripts/comment.py contract.docx \"This cap is too low\" -o annotated.docx\n    85\t```\n    86\t\n    87\tThe script writes `comments.xml`, `commentsExtended.xml`, `commentsIds.xml`, `commentsExtensible.xml`, the relationships, and the content-type overrides. Comment IDs are auto-assigned. It then prints the `<w:commentRangeStart>`/`<w:commentRangeEnd>`/`<w:commentReference>` snippet to add to `word/document.xml` so the comment anchors to specific text \u2014 until you place those markers, the comment exists but is not visible.\n    88\t\n    89\t## Dependencies\n    90\t\n    91\t`docx` (npm, preinstalled \u2014 install only if `require('docx')` fails) \u00b7 `pandoc` \u00b7 LibreOffice (`soffice`) \u00b7 `pdftoppm` (Poppler)\n    92\t",

                                "text": "     1\t---\n     2\tname: pdf\n     3\tdescription: Use this skill whenever the user wants to do anything with PDF files. This includes reading or extracting text/tables from PDFs, combining or merging multiple PDFs into one, splitting PDFs apart, rotating pages, adding watermarks, creating new PDFs, filling PDF forms, encrypting/decrypting PDFs, extracting images, and OCR on scanned PDFs to make them searchable. If the user mentions a .pdf file or asks to produce one, use this skill.\n     4\tlicense: Proprietary. LICENSE.txt has complete terms\n     5\t---\n     6\t\n     7\t# PDF Processing Guide\n     8\t\n     9\t## Overview\n    10\t\n    11\tThis guide covers essential PDF processing operations using Python libraries and command-line tools. For advanced features, JavaScript libraries, and detailed examples, see REFERENCE.md. If you need to fill out a PDF form, read FORMS.md and follow its instructions.\n    12\t\n    13\t## Quick Start\n    14\t\n    15\t```python\n    16\tfrom pypdf import PdfReader, PdfWriter\n    17\t\n    18\t# Read a PDF\n    19\treader = PdfReader(\"document.pdf\")\n    20\tprint(f\"Pages: {len(reader.pages)}\")\n    21\t\n    22\t# Extract text\n    23\ttext = \"\"\n    24\tfor page in reader.pages:\n    25\t    text += page.extract_text()\n    26\t```\n    27\t\n    28\t## Python Libraries\n    29\t\n    30\t### pypdf - Basic Operations\n    31\t\n    32\t#### Merge PDFs\n    33\t```python\n    34\tfrom pypdf import PdfWriter, PdfReader\n    35\t\n    36\twriter = PdfWriter()\n    37\tfor pdf_file in [\"doc1.pdf\", \"doc2.pdf\", \"doc3.pdf\"]:\n    38\t    reader = PdfReader(pdf_file)\n    39\t    for page in reader.pages:\n    40\t        writer.add_page(page)\n    41\t\n    42\twith open(\"merged.pdf\", \"wb\") as output:\n    43\t    writer.write(output)\n    44\t```\n    45\t\n    46\t#### Split PDF\n    47\t```python\n    48\treader = PdfReader(\"input.pdf\")\n    49\tfor i, page in enumerate(reader.pages):\n    50\t    writer = PdfWriter()\n    51\t    writer.add_page(page)\n    52\t    with open(f\"page_{i+1}.pdf\", \"wb\") as output:\n    53\t        writer.write(output)\n    54\t```\n    55\t\n    56\t#### Extract Metadata\n    57\t```python\n    58\treader = PdfReader(\"document.pdf\")\n    59\tmeta = reader.metadata\n    60\tprint(f\"Title: {meta.title}\")\n    61\tprint(f\"Author: {meta.author}\")\n    62\tprint(f\"Subject: {meta.subject}\")\n    63\tprint(f\"Creator: {meta.creator}\")\n    64\t```\n    65\t\n    66\t#### Rotate Pages\n    67\t```python\n    68\treader = PdfReader(\"input.pdf\")\n    69\twriter = PdfWriter()\n    70\t\n    71\tpage = reader.pages[0]\n    72\tpage.rotate(90)  # Rotate 90 degrees clockwise\n    73\twriter.add_page(page)\n    74\t\n    75\twith open(\"rotated.pdf\", \"wb\") as output:\n    76\t    writer.write(output)\n    77\t```\n    78\t\n    79\t### pdfplumber - Text and Table Extraction\n    80\t\n    81\t#### Extract Text with Layout\n    82\t```python\n    83\timport pdfplumber\n    84\t\n    85\twith pdfplumber.open(\"document.pdf\") as pdf:\n    86\t    for page in pdf.pages:\n    87\t        text = page.extract_text()\n    88\t        print(text)\n    89\t```\n    90\t\n    91\t#### Extract Tables\n    92\t```python\n    93\twith pdfplumber.open(\"document.pdf\") as pdf:\n    94\t    for i, page in enumerate(pdf.pages):\n    95\t        tables = page.extract_tables()\n    96\t        for j, table in enumerate(tables):\n    97\t            print(f\"Table {j+1} on page {i+1}:\")\n    98\t            for row in table:\n    99\t                print(row)\n   100\t```\n   101\t\n   102\t#### Advanced Table Extraction\n   103\t```python\n   104\timport pandas as pd\n   105\t\n   106\twith pdfplumber.open(\"document.pdf\") as pdf:\n   107\t    all_tables = []\n   108\t    for page in pdf.pages:\n   109\t        tables = page.extract_tables()\n   110\t        for table in tables:\n   111\t            if table:  # Check if table is not empty\n   112\t                df = pd.DataFrame(table[1:], columns=table[0])\n   113\t                all_tables.append(df)\n   114\t\n   115\t# Combine all tables\n   116\tif all_tables:\n   117\t    combined_df = pd.concat(all_tables, ignore_index=True)\n   118\t    combined_df.to_excel(\"extracted_tables.xlsx\", index=False)\n   119\t```\n   120\t\n   121\t### reportlab - Create PDFs\n   122\t\n   123\t#### Basic PDF Creation\n   124\t```python\n   125\tfrom reportlab.lib.pagesizes import letter\n   126\tfrom reportlab.pdfgen import canvas\n   127\t\n   128\tc = canvas.Canvas(\"hello.pdf\", pagesize=letter)\n   129\twidth, height = letter\n   130\t\n   131\t# Add text\n   132\tc.drawString(100, height - 100, \"Hello World!\")\n   133\tc.drawString(100, height - 120, \"This is a PDF created with reportlab\")\n   134\t\n   135\t# Add a line\n   136\tc.line(100, height - 140, 400, height - 140)\n   137\t\n   138\t# Save\n   139\tc.save()\n   140\t```\n   141\t\n   142\t#### Create PDF with Multiple Pages\n   143\t```python\n   144\tfrom reportlab.lib.pagesizes import letter\n   145\tfrom reportlab.platypus import SimpleDocTemplate, Paragraph, Spacer, PageBreak\n   146\tfrom reportlab.lib.styles import getSampleStyleSheet\n   147\t\n   148\tdoc = SimpleDocTemplate(\"report.pdf\", pagesize=letter)\n   149\tstyles = getSampleStyleSheet()\n   150\tstory = []\n   151\t\n   152\t# Add content\n   153\ttitle = Paragraph(\"Report Title\", styles['Title'])\n   154\tstory.append(title)\n   155\tstory.append(Spacer(1, 12))\n   156\t\n   157\tbody = Paragraph(\"This is the body of the report. \" * 20, styles['Normal'])\n   158\tstory.append(body)\n   159\tstory.append(PageBreak())\n   160\t\n   161\t# Page 2\n   162\tstory.append(Paragraph(\"Page 2\", styles['Heading1']))\n   163\tstory.append(Paragraph(\"Content for page 2\", styles['Normal']))\n   164\t\n   165\t# Build PDF\n   166\tdoc.build(story)\n   167\t```\n   168\t\n   169\t#### Subscripts and Superscripts\n   170\t\n   171\t**IMPORTANT**: Never use Unicode subscript/superscript characters (\u2080\u2081\u2082\u2083\u2084\u2085\u2086\u2087\u2088\u2089, \u2070\u00b9\u00b2\u00b3\u2074\u2075\u2076\u2077\u2078\u2079) in ReportLab PDFs. The built-in fonts do not include these glyphs, causing them to render as solid black boxes.\n   172\t\n   173\tInstead, use ReportLab's XML markup tags in Paragraph objects:\n   174\t```python\n   175\tfrom reportlab.platypus import Paragraph\n   176\tfrom reportlab.lib.styles import getSampleStyleSheet\n   177\t\n   178\tstyles = getSampleStyleSheet()\n   179\t\n   180\t# Subscripts: use <sub> tag\n   181\tchemical = Paragraph(\"H<sub>2</sub>O\", styles['Normal'])\n   182\t\n   183\t# Superscripts: use <super> tag\n   184\tsquared = Paragraph(\"x<super>2</super> + y<super>2</super>\", styles['Normal'])\n   185\t```\n   186\t\n   187\tFor canvas-drawn text (not Paragraph objects), manually adjust font the size and position rather than using Unicode subscripts/superscripts.\n   188\t\n   189\t## Command-Line Tools\n   190\t\n   191\t### pdftotext (poppler-utils)\n   192\t```bash\n   193\t# Extract text\n   194\tpdftotext input.pdf output.txt\n   195\t\n   196\t# Extract text preserving layout\n   197\tpdftotext -layout input.pdf output.txt\n   198\t\n   199\t# Extract specific pages\n   200\tpdftotext -f 1 -l 5 input.pdf output.txt  # Pages 1-5\n   201\t```\n   202\t\n   203\t### qpdf\n   204\t```bash\n   205\t# Merge PDFs\n   206\tqpdf --empty --pages file1.pdf file2.pdf -- merged.pdf\n   207\t\n   208\t# Split pages\n   209\tqpdf input.pdf --pages . 1-5 -- pages1-5.pdf\n   210\tqpdf input.pdf --pages . 6-10 -- pages6-10.pdf\n   211\t\n   212\t# Rotate pages\n   213\tqpdf input.pdf output.pdf --rotate=+90:1  # Rotate page 1 by 90 degrees\n   214\t\n   215\t# Remove password\n   216\tqpdf --password=mypassword --decrypt encrypted.pdf decrypted.pdf\n   217\t```\n   218\t\n   219\t### pdftk (if available)\n   220\t```bash\n   221\t# Merge\n   222\tpdftk file1.pdf file2.pdf cat output merged.pdf\n   223\t\n   224\t# Split\n   225\tpdftk input.pdf burst\n   226\t\n   227\t# Rotate\n   228\tpdftk input.pdf rotate 1east output rotated.pdf\n   229\t```\n   230\t\n   231\t## Common Tasks\n   232\t\n   233\t### Extract Text from Scanned PDFs\n   234\t```python\n   235\t# Requires: pip install pytesseract pdf2image\n   236\timport pytesseract\n   237\tfrom pdf2image import convert_from_path\n   238\t\n   239\t# Convert PDF to images\n   240\timages = convert_from_path('scanned.pdf')\n   241\t\n   242\t# OCR each page\n   243\ttext = \"\"\n   244\tfor i, image in enumerate(images):\n   245\t    text += f\"Page {i+1}:\\n\"\n   246\t    text += pytesseract.image_to_string(image)\n   247\t    text += \"\\n\\n\"\n   248\t\n   249\tprint(text)\n   250\t```\n   251\t\n   252\t### Add Watermark\n   253\t```python\n   254\tfrom pypdf import PdfReader, PdfWriter\n   255\t\n   256\t# Create watermark (or load existing)\n   257\twatermark = PdfReader(\"watermark.pdf\").pages[0]\n   258\t\n   259\t# Apply to all pages\n   260\treader = PdfReader(\"document.pdf\")\n   261\twriter = PdfWriter()\n   262\t\n   263\tfor page in reader.pages:\n   264\t    page.merge_page(watermark)\n   265\t    writer.add_page(page)\n   266\t\n   267\twith open(\"watermarked.pdf\", \"wb\") as output:\n   268\t    writer.write(output)\n   269\t```\n   270\t\n   271\t### Extract Images\n   272\t```bash\n   273\t# Using pdfimages (poppler-utils)\n   274\tpdfimages -j input.pdf output_prefix\n   275\t\n   276\t# This extracts all images as output_prefix-000.jpg, output_prefix-001.jpg, etc.\n   277\t```\n   278\t\n   279\t### Password Protection\n   280\t```python\n   281\tfrom pypdf import PdfReader, PdfWriter\n   282\t\n   283\treader = PdfReader(\"input.pdf\")\n   284\twriter = PdfWriter()\n   285\t\n   286\tfor page in reader.pages:\n   287\t    writer.add_page(page)\n   288\t\n   289\t# Add password\n   290\twriter.encrypt(\"userpassword\", \"ownerpassword\")\n   291\t\n   292\twith open(\"encrypted.pdf\", \"wb\") as output:\n   293\t    writer.write(output)\n   294\t```\n   295\t\n   296\t## Quick Reference\n   297\t\n   298\t| Task | Best Tool | Command/Code |\n   299\t|------|-----------|--------------|\n   300\t| Merge PDFs | pypdf | `writer.add_page(page)` |\n   301\t| Split PDFs | pypdf | One page per file |\n   302\t| Extract text | pdfplumber | `page.extract_text()` |\n   303\t| Extract tables | pdfplumber | `page.extract_tables()` |\n   304\t| Create PDFs | reportlab | Canvas or Platypus |\n   305\t| Command line merge | qpdf | `qpdf --empty --pages ...` |\n   306\t| OCR scanned PDFs | pytesseract | Convert to image first |\n   307\t| Fill PDF forms | pdf-lib or pypdf (see FORMS.md) | See FORMS.md |\n   308\t\n   309\t## Next Steps\n   310\t\n   311\t- For advanced pypdfium2 usage, see REFERENCE.md\n   312\t- For JavaScript libraries (pdf-lib), see REFERENCE.md\n   313\t- If you need to fill out a PDF form, follow the instructions in FORMS.md\n   314\t- For troubleshooting guides, see REFERENCE.md\n   315\t",
